name: OpenAI
description: Leading AI lab (ChatGPT, GPT models) whose massive compute purchasing and custom silicon ambitions reshape chip demand
threat: OpenAI's push for custom inference silicon (with Broadcom) and alternative chip suppliers (Cerebras, AMD) threatens to diversify demand away from pure Nvidia dependence while its scale validates the entire AI-chip buildout.

name: Anthropic
description: AI safety-focused lab (Claude models) with massive multi-cloud compute commitments across chip vendors
threat: Anthropic's diversified compute strategy across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, and Nvidia GPUs pressures Nvidia's pricing power and validates alternative accelerator architectures at hyperscale.

name: xAI
description: Elon Musk's AI lab (Grok models) building some of the world's largest GPU clusters (Colossus)
threat: xAI's rapid buildout of the largest GPU clusters in the world is one of Nvidia's single biggest demand drivers, while its interest in alternative silicon signals future diversification risk.

name: Cerebras Systems
description: Maker of wafer-scale AI chips (WSE-3) for ultra-fast inference, now publicly traded after May 2026 IPO
threat: Cerebras's wafer-scale architecture beat Nvidia on single-user inference speed and landed a $10B OpenAI compute deal, proving non-GPU inference architectures can win at hyperscale before Cerebras itself went public.

name: Groq
description: Inference-chip pioneer (LPU) pivoting to an inference-cloud operator after licensing its core IP to Nvidia
threat: Nvidia's reported $20B non-exclusive licensing deal for Groq's LPU technology both validates fast-inference architecture as a real threat and shows Nvidia absorbing rather than losing to non-GPU challengers.

name: SambaNova Systems
description: AI chipmaker (SN40L/SN50) focused on inference chips and on-premise enterprise AI deployments
threat: SambaNova's on-premise inference chips and near-acquisition talks with Intel highlight both real enterprise demand for Nvidia alternatives and the difficulty of independently scaling against Nvidia's ecosystem lock-in.

name: Tenstorrent
description: Jim Keller-led AI chip designer building discrete, workstation-scale AI accelerators, reportedly in acquisition talks with Qualcomm
last_round: Reported $8-10B acquisition talks with Qualcomm, Jul 2026 (prior: sought $3.2B valuation round, Nov 2025)
threat: Qualcomm's reported bid for Tenstorrent at up to $10B signals large semiconductor incumbents see standalone AI-chip IP as strategically necessary, validating the broader non-Nvidia accelerator thesis.

name: Etched
description: Builder of transformer-specific ASICs (Sohu chip) designed exclusively to accelerate transformer-model inference
threat: Etched's bet that a transformer-only ASIC can dramatically outperform general-purpose GPUs on cost-per-token is a direct wager against Nvidia's flexible-architecture moat.

name: Fermi America
description: Developer of the world's largest private, behind-the-meter nuclear-and-gas power grid and AI data-center campus in Texas
threat: Fermi's plan to build a private, off-grid multi-gigawatt power campus (nuclear, gas, solar, storage) competing directly for hyperscaler tenants threatens to disintermediate incumbent regulated utilities and IPPs from AI power contracts.

name: Valar Atomics
description: Developer of standardized, mass-manufactured waterless small modular nuclear reactors for AI data centers
threat: Valar's factory-built waterless reactors, already powering an Nvidia Blackwell cluster in partnership with Nvidia, threaten to undercut incumbent generators on speed-to-power for AI campuses.

name: Blue Energy Global
description: Startup building grid-scale nuclear reactors constructed in shipyards to cut cost and schedule for data-center power
threat: Blue Energy's shipyard-manufacturing model for 1.5GW reactors targets the same speed-to-power gap that has driven utilities and IPPs to underbuild for AI demand, offering a faster alternative supply route.

name: Antares Nuclear
description: Small modular reactor developer targeting U.S. military bases and price-insensitive critical infrastructure customers
threat: Antares's Pentagon-backed SMR contracts show private nuclear capital increasingly bypassing traditional utility procurement, creating an alternative power-supply track for critical AI and defense loads.

name: Crusoe Energy
description: Vertically integrated 'AI factory' company combining rapid energy sourcing, data-center construction, and cloud services (developer behind Stargate Abilene)
last_round: $1.375B Series E (equity, Oct 2025) plus $11.6B debt/equity phase-two (May 2026)
total_raised: $3B+ equity, plus tens of billions in project debt
threat: Crusoe's model of bundling power sourcing with data-center construction lets hyperscalers skip traditional utility interconnection queues, threatening to route gigawatts of new demand around incumbent grid operators and IPPs.

name: CoreWeave
description: GPU-cloud operator whose massive power procurement and financing structures underpin the AI-infrastructure debt market (note: now publicly traded, included for power-market relevance)
stage: publicly traded (IPO Mar 2025), power/financing model still disrupting sector
threat: CoreWeave's GPU-backed, investment-grade financing structure lets it lock up 1.7GW of active power capacity via bankruptcy-remote SPVs, a template competitors and IPPs must now match to win hyperscaler leases.

name: Vantage Data Centers
description: Private data-center developer building multi-gigawatt AI campuses (Stargate Frontier, Lighthouse) financed via infrastructure debt
last_round: $25B Frontier campus commitment, 2026 (project financing, not corporate equity round)
total_raised: tens of billions in project-level debt and equity since 2020
threat: Vantage's ability to finance and deliver 1,000+ MW campuses within a single year outpaces the buildout cadence of regulated utilities, forcing incumbents to accelerate capacity additions or lose hyperscaler tenants.

name: TerraPower
description: Bill Gates-backed developer of next-generation Natrium sodium-fast nuclear reactors for industrial and tech customers
last_round: Undisclosed growth funding, ongoing (DOE-backed demonstration project in Wyoming)
threat: TerraPower's advanced Natrium reactor, backed by Amazon and Bill Gates, positions next-gen nuclear as a long-horizon threat to gas-peaker and traditional nuclear operators competing for AI baseload contracts.

name: Anduril Industries
description: Vertically integrated defense company building autonomous drones, munitions, and software (Lattice OS) for the US military and allies
threat: Anduril's software-defined, mass-manufactured autonomy platforms directly threaten legacy primes' cost-plus hardware model while validating investor appetite for defense disruption at massive scale.

name: Shield AI
description: Maker of Hivemind autonomy software and X-Bat autonomous aircraft for contested-environment drone operations
threat: Selection for the US Air Force Collaborative Combat Aircraft program shows autonomy software startups can win prime roles on next-gen fighter drone programs traditionally reserved for LMT/RTX.

name: Saronic Technologies
description: Builder of autonomous surface vessels (Marauder-class) for naval defense and maritime autonomy at scale
threat: Saronic's rapid unmanned-vessel production (targeting 20+ ships/year) directly challenges traditional shipbuilders and primes for Navy uncrewed surface vessel programs at a fraction of legacy cost and schedule.

name: Helsing
description: Munich-based European defense AI company building software for drones, aircraft, and submarines for NATO militaries
threat: As Europe's largest defense startup pushing 'sovereign AI,' Helsing threatens US primes' access to European rearmament budgets and validates AI-native defense software as a category outside the US market.

name: Epirus
description: Maker of Leonidas high-power microwave counter-drone directed-energy weapon systems
threat: Epirus' directed-energy counter-swarm systems offer a cheaper, scalable alternative to missile-based air defense sold by RTX and LMT, addressing the drone-saturation threat exposed in recent conflicts.

name: Castelion
description: SpaceX-alumni-founded startup mass-producing low-cost hypersonic strike weapons (Blackbeard)
threat: Castelion's commercial-style rapid iteration on hypersonic munitions challenges LMT/RTX's historic monopoly on hypersonic weapons development and could undercut their unit economics on future contracts.

name: Applied Intuition
description: Vehicle intelligence/simulation software company expanding into defense autonomy (Axion, Acuity) via EpiSci acquisition
threat: Applied Intuition's push from autonomous-vehicle simulation into defense autonomy software threatens to displace prime-built mission software and simulation environments used across LMT/RTX programs.

name: Skydio
description: US-made autonomous drone manufacturer serving enterprise, public safety, and defense customers, positioned against DJI
threat: Skydio's domestic manufacturing scale and regulatory tailwinds from Chinese-drone bans directly erode AeroVironment's small-drone market share in public safety and defense.

name: SpaceX
description: Dominant launch, Starlink satellite broadband, and Starship deep-space company preparing for a landmark IPO
threat: SpaceX's Starlink and Starship dominance dwarfs every public space comp combined, and its pending IPO (targeting up to $800B+ valuation) will reset the entire sector's valuation benchmarks overnight.

name: Stoke Space
description: Developer of the fully and rapidly reusable Nova medium-lift launch vehicle at Cape Canaveral
last_round: $860M Series D, Feb 2026 (in process of raising ~$1B further, Aug 2026)
threat: Stoke's fully reusable Nova rocket, backed by a rising ~$9B valuation, directly targets Rocket Lab's and legacy primes' medium-lift launch market with a SpaceX-style reusability model.

name: K2 Space
description: Manufacturer of large, high-power satellite buses for commercial and defense constellations
threat: K2's high-power large-satellite platforms compete directly with Iridium's and AST SpaceMobile's next-gen constellation hardware, and its rapid production model threatens legacy satellite bus suppliers.

name: True Anomaly
description: Builder of autonomous spacecraft and space-based interceptors for space domain awareness and Golden Dome missile defense
threat: True Anomaly's space-interceptor role in the Golden Dome missile-defense program positions it to capture national security space budgets that would otherwise flow to Boeing and legacy space-defense primes.

name: Impulse Space
description: Builder of orbital transfer vehicles ('space tugs') for in-space mobility, founded by SpaceX propulsion veteran Tom Mueller
threat: Impulse Space's orbital mobility infrastructure threatens to become the default 'last mile' layer for satellite deployment, disintermediating launch providers like Rocket Lab from higher-margin orbit-raising services.

name: Apex Space
description: Mass-manufacturer of productized, configurable satellite bus platforms (Aries, Nova, Comet) for commercial and defense payloads
threat: Apex's high-rate, standardized satellite bus production model undercuts custom-built satellite platforms, threatening incumbent suppliers' margins as Pentagon demand for rapid constellation deployment grows.

name: Varda Space Industries
description: Operator of reentry capsules for microgravity manufacturing (pharmaceuticals) and hypersonics testing
threat: Varda's reentry-capsule and in-space manufacturing niche opens a new commercial space revenue category (pharma manufacturing, hypersonics testing) that diversifies demand beyond launch, indirectly pressuring Rocket Lab's reentry ambitions.

name: Axiom Space
description: Developer of commercial space station (Axiom Station) and NASA spacesuits (AxEMU) as ISS successor
threat: Axiom's role as the leading ISS-successor commercial station builder directly challenges Boeing's legacy human-spaceflight infrastructure position as NASA transitions off the ISS by 2030.

name: Figure AI
description: Developer of general-purpose humanoid robots (Figure 03) for logistics, manufacturing and eventually home use
threat: At a $39B valuation and backed by Nvidia and Brookfield, Figure directly threatens to leapfrog traditional industrial automation and warehouse robotics incumbents with general-purpose humanoids.

name: Physical Intelligence
description: Builds general-purpose AI foundation models ('robot brains') that can control many different robot bodies
last_round: $600M, Nov 2025 (in talks for ~$1B more at >$11B, Mar 2026)
threat: Its foundation-model 'brain' approach could commoditize the control software layer that industrial automation vendors like Rockwell and Fanuc currently bundle with their hardware.

name: Skild AI
description: Builds an 'omni-bodied' foundation model (Skild Brain) designed to operate any robot for any task across industrial and commercial settings
threat: Skild's revenue-generating omni-bodied brain, already deployed in warehouses, manufacturing and data centers, threatens to displace proprietary robot-control software sold by industrial automation incumbents.

name: Apptronik
description: Austin-based maker of the Apollo humanoid robot for factories, warehouses and logistics, partnered with Google DeepMind
threat: Apollo is already piloting in Mercedes-Benz and GXO Logistics facilities, positioning Apptronik to beat Tesla Optimus and Chinese humanoids to commercial warehouse/factory deployment ahead of incumbents like Rockwell and Symbotic.

name: 1X Technologies
description: Norwegian, OpenAI-backed maker of the NEO bipedal humanoid robot targeting home and enterprise (logistics, guarding) use
threat: 1X's consumer-home NEO strategy, backed directly by OpenAI, opens an entirely new physical-AI market beyond industrial floors that none of the public comps currently address.

name: Agility Robotics
description: Maker of the Digit bipedal warehouse/logistics humanoid robot, going public via SPAC merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI
threat: As the first pure-play humanoid robotics company to go public, Agility validates warehouse-humanoid economics deployed at Amazon, Toyota and GXO sites, directly threatening Symbotic and Zebra's warehouse automation stacks.

name: Neura Robotics
description: German full-stack cognitive robotics company building humanoid (4NE1) and industrial robots plus the Neuraverse shared-intelligence platform
threat: Backed by major tech and industrial investors, Neura is Europe's best-funded physical-AI challenger to Fanuc- and Rockwell-style industrial automation incumbents.

name: Unitree Robotics
description: Hangzhou-based maker of humanoid robots and quadruped robot dogs, mainland China's first listed humanoid-robot company
total_raised: IPO plus prior VC rounds from Geely, Alibaba, Tencent
threat: Unitree's profitable, low-cost humanoid production model and fresh public capital threaten to undercut Western and Japanese robotics incumbents on price at scale.
